instruction: Set up git so that the user.name is 'TestUser' to enable committing changes.

command: import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'alt', 't'); time.sleep(0.5)

result.command: git config --global user.name 2>/dev/null | grep -qx 'TestUser' && echo 1 || echo 0

metadata.explanation: Task requires configuring git user.name setting by running 'git config --global user.name TestUser'. The evaluator checks if 'git config --global user.name' returns a value containing 'TestUser' (returns 1 if found, 0 if not). Expected result is '1\n' indicating the git user.name was set. This is similar in complexity to the original conda task - both involve configuring tools through command-line configuration.
metadata.verification: Verified by checking command structure: 'git config --global user.name' retrieves the configured username, grep checks if it contains 'TestUser', and the shell expression returns 1 if found (exit code 0), 0 if not found (non-zero exit code). The exact_match metric compares this output against expected '1\n'.

llm_judge_reasons: The verification command correctly uses 'grep -qx TestUser' which performs exact line matching, ensuring user.name must be exactly 'TestUser' (not a substring like 'TestUser123' or 'MyTestUser').
The getter correctly extracts git config state via 'git config --global user.name 2>/dev/null'.
The command logic correctly returns '1' when the exact value matches and '0' otherwise.
The metric 'exact_match' correctly compares the result '1\n' against expected '1\n'.
